intro: An AI assistant for speechwriters helps you draft, research and revise a speech by voice, so you spend less time on lookups and more on the words. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that sees your screen, answers out loud and types text where your cursor sits. This page shows how that fits a speechwriter's week, where the limits are, and what to check first.

blocks.text: Speechwriting means writing in someone else's voice, then checking that the words sound right out loud. Most of the day goes to drafts and revisions, plus the messages around them. The Bureau of Labor Statistics files speechwriters under its Writers and Authors profile. It notes that speeches are delivered live, so the writer must consider how the audience will react.
Where the time goes in a speechwriter's week

Nobody has measured how speechwriters split their hours. The research checked for this page found no study of speechwriters' time or the apps they use. So the figures below describe knowledge work in general. Use them as a starting point, then track your own week for a few days.

Microsoft's June 2025 study found that the average employee receives 117 emails and 153 Teams messages a day. The same study counts 275 interruptions, roughly one every two minutes, from meetings, email and chat notifications. Booher's survey found that 42% of knowledge workers spend 3 hours or more a day reading and writing email.

A speechwriting office adds its own traffic. Requests come from the principal, communications staff, policy advisers and event planners, often with different deadlines. Several people may want a change to the same paragraph on the same afternoon. Write down who can edit a draft and who must approve it. That short list saves time whatever tool you use.

blocks.title: Read the numbers with care
blocks.text: The BLS pay figures and the survey numbers describe all writers, or all knowledge workers. They are not speechwriter data. Use them as context, and track your own hours before you plan around them.
Small lookups that break a draft

Most interruptions inside a draft are small. You need the exact title of a bill, the spelling of a donor's name, the date of a visit, or the menu path to a Word feature. Each lookup pulls you out of the sentence you were writing. Getting back into that sentence can take longer than the lookup itself.

Lazur handles these lookups by voice, without leaving the document. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask where something is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on.

items: Where is it? Hold ⌥⌘ and ask. Lazur circles the item on screen and labels it.

What is on this page? Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud.
What did I ask earlier? Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, kept on your Mac.

blocks.text: How to dictate speech drafts with fn in any app

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Speak the draft the way you would deliver it, in full sentences. Then read the result on screen. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans, so you can draft aloud as often as you need.

Three features help with speech work. Snippets hold boilerplate you reuse, such as an opening greeting, a thank-you line or a standard sign-off. The personal dictionary holds names and terms the tool tends to get wrong, such as a minister's name or a program title. Clipboard slots keep approved sentences ready to paste.
Speaking a first pass usually gets you closer than typing one. The sentences come out the way you talk. Expect the errors to cluster in names, numbers and dates, and fix those by hand.

blocks.title: Read it aloud before it moves
blocks.text: Dictated text reads well until you hear it. Read each draft aloud before it reaches the principal. Check every figure against its source, not against the draft that quotes it.
Word and Google Docs features speechwriters look up most

Word and Google Docs hide useful features in menus, and the menus change between versions. In Google Docs, word count sits under Tools > Word count, and ⌘⇧C opens the same count. The [word count guide](/how-to/see-word-count-in-google-docs) covers both routes. Check the length of a draft before you rehearse it.

In Word for Mac, track changes lives on the Review tab, under Review > Track Changes. The [Word guide for speechwriters](/for/speechwriters/word) walks through drafting, cutting and reading aloud. If a menu has moved since the last update, hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur where it went.

Comments and suggestions cause their own mistakes. A note in the margin can change a sentence you already fixed. Read the whole thread before you accept any change. The guides on [adding a comment in Word](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-word) and [accepting or rejecting suggestions in Google Docs](/how-to/accept-or-reject-suggestions-in-google-docs) cover the steps.
Research a speech without losing the source

Speeches need facts that hold up. A wrong date, a made-up quote or a stale statistic can cost the principal credibility on stage. Lazur's research runs in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It returns a summary and a report. Treat the summary as a list of leads, not as a source.

Here is a worked example. The principal wants one line about the history of a housing bill. Ask Lazur to research the bill and cite its sources. Open each cited page yourself. Confirm the date, the sponsor and the exact wording. Copy only what you checked into the draft, and keep the link beside it.
Keep a source list next to the draft. Every line that holds a fact gets a link. When someone asks where a number came from, you answer in seconds instead of searching your inbox.
Check your Office for Mac version before a deadline

Old builds miss fixes, and support ends on a schedule. Microsoft's update history lists version 16.114.4 (26110224) as the latest Office for Mac build, released November 4, 2026. It also shows that Office 2019 for Mac reached end of support on October 10, 2023.

Office 2021 is less clear. Microsoft's lifecycle page gives October 14, 2026 as its retirement date, and that date has already passed. A Microsoft known-issues note mentions a separate reduced-functionality date on macOS. We did not open the page behind that note, so check Microsoft's pages before you plan around any date.
To find your version, open Word > About Word. Write the version down before a deadline, not during one. If your office standardizes on one version, ask IT which one it is.
Protect unreleased remarks and follow office rules

Unreleased speeches often contain policy changes, personnel details or negotiation positions. Your employer decides which tools may handle that text. Follow those rules, even when a chat window feels like a notepad. Ask your communications or legal team before you paste or dictate unreleased remarks into any AI tool. This page makes no compliance claims for Lazur, and it cannot make them for your office.

Lazur's privacy terms are simple to state. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Read the full terms, then decide with your office's rules in mind.

blocks.title: When in doubt, keep it general
blocks.text: If your office has not approved a tool for unreleased text, describe the task in general words. Ask for structure, rhythm or cuts, and keep the sensitive facts out of the prompt.
Mistakes that cost speechwriters time

items: Using a quote the tool produced without checking it against a source.
Letting the tool set the voice. Start from the principal's own phrases and fix the rhythm by ear.
Dictating a draft and skipping the read-aloud pass.
Treating a research summary as the source for a date, figure or name.
Pasting unreleased remarks into an AI tool before checking your office's rules.
Hunting through menus for something one hold-and-ask would find.

blocks.text: A realistic speechwriting day with Lazur
The example day is an illustration. The times and phrases are examples, not data from a study. Each line shows what you might say and what Lazur does with it. Use the same pattern for your own week.
Set up Lazur for a speechwriting week

Start with the free trial. It needs no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app. [Download Lazur](/download) for macOS, on Apple silicon or Intel. When macOS asks for permission to hear you and see your screen, allow it. Lazur needs both to work.

Practice the two hold keys before a deadline. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about the screen. Hold fn to dictate at the cursor. Test each one in a scratch document, not in a draft you need. Then add your names and terms to the personal dictionary, and save your standard lines as snippets.
Compare the [pricing page](/pricing) before you commit. Plans differ in AI actions per month, and dictation is unlimited on both. Check the page for current prices, since prices can change.

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for speechwriters?
faq.answer: It is a tool that helps you draft, research and revise speeches, usually by voice. Lazur does this on a Mac. Hold a key and talk. It answers out loud, points at things on your screen and types text where your cursor sits.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant write the speech for me?
faq.answer: It can draft a first pass or a shorter version of a paragraph. The voice, the choices and the final sign-off still belong to you and the principal. Read every line aloud, and check every fact against a source before it goes out.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Word and Google Docs?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app on macOS, including Word and Google Docs. It is not a plugin or add-in for either one. It points at menu items, answers questions about the screen and types dictated text at the cursor. It does not click buttons for you.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI on an unreleased speech?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Your office decides what is allowed, and this page makes no compliance claims.

faq.question: How does Lazur handle research for a speech?
faq.answer: Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. You get a summary and a report. Open each cited source yourself, confirm the wording and the date, then use only what you checked.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: How much does it cost, and is there a trial?
faq.answer: There is a free trial with no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app. The Pro and Power plans differ in AI actions per month. Dictation is unlimited on both. Check the pricing page for current prices.

painPoints.text: Microsoft's June 2025 study counts 117 emails and 153 Teams messages a day for the average knowledge worker. A speechwriting office adds requests on top, often with changes from several people.

painPoints.title: Interruptions chop the draft into pieces
painPoints.text: The same study counts 275 interruptions a day, roughly one every two minutes. A paragraph that needs quiet time gets written in short sittings, and the thread gets lost between them.

painPoints.title: Email can take the afternoon
painPoints.text: Booher's survey found that 42% of knowledge workers spend 3 hours or more a day reading and writing email. Drafting often has to fit around that time.

painPoints.title: Lookups break the sentence
painPoints.text: A name, a date, a bill number or a Word menu path pulls you out of the draft. Each detour makes it harder to get back into the rhythm of the sentence.

painPoints.title: Live delivery raises the stakes
painPoints.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics says speechwriters write for live delivery, so they must think about how the audience will react. A wrong name or date is heard the moment it is spoken.
